app_subtitle: Smart crop finance for Indian farmers
schemes_header: Government Schemes You May Qualify For
why_cost_text: This estimate is based on average input costs (seed, fertilizer, labour, irrigation, and other expenses) for your crop, state, and season from government cultivation cost data. You can edit individual items above.
why_profit_text: Profit scenarios use historical yield and price data. Good harvest uses the 75th percentile, normal uses the median, and poor uses the 25th percentile for both yield and price. Actual results may vary.
why_breakeven_text: Break-even price is the minimum selling price needed to cover your total input costs, calculated as: Total Cost ÷ Expected Yield (quintals). Selling above this price means profit.
why_risk_text: Risk is measured using the Coefficient of Variation (CV) of historical yields and prices. Higher variation means higher risk. Green = low risk, Yellow = medium risk, Red = high risk.
why_dscr_text: The Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) compares your expected normal harvest income to your total loan repayment amount. A DSCR above 1.25 is considered safe; below 1.0 is a warning sign.
why_funding_gap_text: Funding gap = Total Cost − Own Capital. This is the amount you need to borrow. The KCC limit reduces this gap; any remaining amount is the residual gap you need to arrange separately.
why_lender_comparison_text: Interest is calculated using simple interest: Principal × Annual Rate × Months ÷ 12. The same formula is applied to all three lenders so only the rate differs. KCC rates are subsidized by the government.
why_msp_text: MSP (Minimum Support Price) is the government-guaranteed minimum price for your crop. If the market price falls below MSP, the government is supposed to procure at MSP. Selling above MSP is better.
scheme_kcc_desc: Low-interest revolving credit for crop inputs and allied activities. Eligible for all farmers with land ownership or lease documents.
scheme_pmkisan_desc: ₹6,000 per year direct income support in three installments of ₹2,000 each. Eligible for small and marginal farmers with cultivable land.
scheme_pmfby_desc: Subsidized crop insurance covering losses from natural calamities, pests, and diseases. Premium is 2% for Kharif and 1.5% for Rabi crops.
scheme_kcc_benefit: Get credit at just 4% per year (after subvention) for seeds, fertilizer, labour, and other crop costs.
scheme_kcc_eligibility_1: Farmer must own or lease agricultural land.
scheme_kcc_eligibility_2: All crop types are covered — no crop restriction at national level.
scheme_kcc_eligibility_3: Sharecroppers and tenant farmers with valid lease documents are also eligible.
scheme_kcc_documents: Land ownership / lease document, Aadhaar card, passport-size photo, bank account details.
scheme_kcc_where_to_apply: Nearest public sector bank, regional rural bank (RRB), or primary agricultural credit society (PACS).
scheme_kcc_verify_note: Verify on official site — rules last verified: see config.
scheme_kcc_eligible: You appear eligible for KCC based on your land size.
scheme_kcc_ineligible_no_land: KCC requires land ownership or a valid lease document.
scheme_kcc_ineligible_land_too_large: Land size is above the system limit — verify eligibility directly with your bank.
scheme_pmkisan_benefit: Receive ₹6,000 per year directly into your bank account in three installments of ₹2,000.
scheme_pmkisan_eligibility_1: Must be a farmer family with cultivable land in their name.
scheme_pmkisan_eligibility_2: Land holding up to 5 acres (PLACEHOLDER – verify current rules on portal).
scheme_pmkisan_eligibility_3: Institutional land holders, serving/retired government employees, and income-tax payers are excluded.
scheme_pmkisan_documents: Aadhaar card, bank account passbook (linked to Aadhaar), land records (Patta / Khata).
scheme_pmkisan_where_to_apply: Visit the official PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) or contact your local Common Service Centre (CSC) or Village Revenue Officer.
scheme_pmkisan_verify_note: Verify on official site — rules last verified: see config.
scheme_pmkisan_eligible: You appear eligible for PM-KISAN based on your land size.
scheme_pmkisan_ineligible_no_land: PM-KISAN requires cultivable land registered in the farmer's name.
scheme_pmkisan_ineligible_land_too_large: Your land holding may exceed the PM-KISAN limit (PLACEHOLDER – verify on portal).
scheme_pmfby_benefit: Get insurance coverage for your crop at a premium of only 2% (Kharif) or 1.5% (Rabi) of the sum insured.
scheme_pmfby_eligibility_1: Must grow a notified crop in a notified area for that season.
scheme_pmfby_eligibility_2: Both loanee and non-loanee farmers are eligible.
scheme_pmfby_eligibility_3: Enroll before the cut-off date for your season (typically 2 weeks before sowing).
scheme_pmfby_documents: Land record / lease document, bank account details, sowing certificate (if available), Aadhaar card.
scheme_pmfby_where_to_apply: Enroll through your bank, insurance company agent, or the PMFBY portal (pmfby.gov.in).
scheme_pmfby_verify_note: Verify on official site — rules last verified: see config.
scheme_pmfby_eligible: Your crop and season appear covered under PMFBY.
scheme_pmfby_ineligible_crop_not_covered: Your crop is not in the list of PMFBY-covered crops (PLACEHOLDER – verify with your state agriculture department).
scheme_pmfby_ineligible_season_not_cover: PMFBY coverage is not listed for this season. Summer crops are generally not covered.
